title: Electron 'Night Owls Never Sleep' (StriX Launch 14)
t0_note: Rocket Lab mission page window open / NET 1:00 p.m. NZDT = 2026-11-27T00:00:00Z. SOURCE CONFLICT recorded in index.json: the same company's launch-safety page prints NET 00:05 UTC | 13:00 NZDT (those two clocks disagree with each other; 13:00 NZDT is 00:00Z), and LL2 2093e4fc-ac8c-4296-a1b5-deececee6a72 lists NET 00:05Z, window 00:00-00:05Z, last_updated 2026-11-20T06:34:05Z. T0 is the mission-page 00:00Z.

pad.src: https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/2093e4fc-ac8c-4296-a1b5-deececee6a72/ (LL2 'Unknown Pad', Rocket Lab LC-1 Mahia). Elevation is not on that record; 0 m is an ASSUMPTION. Launch-safety page says Launch Complex 1 and does not say pad A or B.

azimuth_deg.derived: Mean of great-circle bearings from this pad to the vertex-average centroids of NAVAREA XIV 338/26 space-debris areas A and B (daily 1615-0130Z, 26 Nov-10 Dec 2026, which covers 2026-11-27T00:00Z). Area A vertices 37-42.00S 177-18.00W, 37-00.00S 173-12.00W, 38-36.00S 172-48.00W, 39-18.00S 176-57.00W: centroid 38.1500S 175.0625W, bearing 80.85 deg, 626 km. Area B vertices 35-36.00S 165-48.00W, 34-24.00S 161-00.00W, 36-00.00S 160-18.00W, 37-18.00S 165-24.00W: centroid 35.8250S 163.1250W, bearing 83.10 deg, 1716 km. Mean of the unrounded bearings is 81.97 deg. The near-field marine box on NZ Coastal 306/26 and the Rocket Lab launch-safety page (around the pad, ~25 km) was not used. Non-rotating inclination from 81.97 deg is 39.94 deg. Rocket Lab publishes 38 deg. sin(az)=cos(38)/cos(39.260881) is 1.018, so 38 deg is below the non-rotating floor set by the pad latitude (39.26 deg) and was not used to replace the hazard azimuth.

payload_kg.assumption: Synspective's StriX page lists the satellite as '100kg class', not a weighed mass for Launch 14. Kick Stage dry 40 kg is the Electron user-guide figure used on electron-iqps10. Kick propellant ~50 kg is ASSUMED. 100+40+50=190, the same stack accounting as electron-iqps10. Not fitted and not an estimate of this flight.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: S2 inserts the Kick Stage into a 'low elliptical orbit' (Electron user guide). Perigee ASSUMED 230 km, the same assumption as electron-iqps10 and electron-hawkeye360. Not this flight's element.

header_notes: UNTUNED: Rocket Lab has published no mission timeline for Night Owls Never Sleep. Electron Payload User Guide 8.0 generic event times are the hard times (S1 cutoff L+155 s, S2 ignition L+162 s, fairing L+184 s, S2 cutoff L+535 s).

T0 is the mission-page window open 2026-11-27T00:00:00Z (1:00 p.m. NZDT). SOURCE CONFLICT: launch-safety page prints NET 00:05 UTC and 13:00 NZDT, which are not the same instant; LL2 NET is 00:05Z with window 00:00-00:05Z. Those were not used as T0.

Inclination 38 deg is published by Rocket Lab. Azimuth 81.97 deg is the mean bearing to NAVAREA XIV 338/26 debris areas A and B. Non-rotating inclination from that azimuth is 39.94 deg. 38 deg is below the pad latitude, so it is not a reachable non-rotating heading. Azimuth was not retuned.
Single StriX SAR satellite for Synspective. Payload 190 kg is the ASSUMED stack (100 kg class + Kick Stage), not a fit.
File ends 2 revs after S2 cutoff on the inferred insertion orbit. Rocket Lab publishes no deploy time and no Kick Stage burn time for this mission. Kick Stage circularization is not modelled.

deploy.note: Rocket Lab's Night Owls Never Sleep mission page and launch-safety page publish no deploy time and no Kick Stage burn time (orbit, inclination, window and hazard areas only, checked 2026-11-24); propagated 2 revs on the inferred insertion orbit

drag.basis: ASSUMPTION: free-molecular Cd 2.2, frontal area of the 1.2 m-diameter upper stage, the same coast drag as electron-iqps10
